intended_object: A helper for the library's Kurosh subgroup theorem proof. It lifts the orbit-projection prefunctor (raw Bass–Serre vertex quiver → symmetrized orbit quiver) to the symmetrized source quiver, so that paths in the Bass–Serre graph map to paths in the quotient graph. I inferred this from the docstring and from how it is used right afterwards (via `mapPath`, to show that the quotient is connected).
explanation: The body just applies Mathlib's `Quiver.Symmetrify.lift` to `rawBassSerreOrbitPrefunctorToSymm`. That extends the edge map so it also handles reversed edges. It is internal plumbing: in lines 1146–1153 it is only used to push paths through `mapPath` when proving that the orbit (quotient) graph is connected. In informal mathematics this step is just "the quotient map of a graph sends paths to paths". It is not a mathematical concept defined in its own right that one could check against the literature, so it counts as a technical device.
